name: Relativistic kinetic energy
seoDesc: Relativistic kinetic energy: work out mass from the velocity and the kinetic energy. A free physics calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Give the Relativistic kinetic energy calculator the velocity and the kinetic energy and it returns mass. It is built for a lab report, a problem set or a sanity check on a physical situation. Nothing is submitted anywhere: the arithmetic runs in the page you are looking at.

sections.title: How does the Relativistic kinetic energy calculator work?
sections.html:
The Relativistic kinetic energy calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports mass in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the velocity and the kinetic energy.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A measured quantity, entered by default in light speed. The unit chip switches it to any of the 25 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in 10¹² of joules. The unit chip switches it to any of the 33 supported units.

sections.title: The formula behind the Relativistic kinetic energy calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

Mass=-kinetic energy × the square root of (89875517873681764 − (velocity ^ 2)) ÷ (89875517873681764 × the square root of (89875517873681764 − (velocity ^ 2)) − 26944002417373989539335912)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• Shown in kilograms, and convertible to any of the 29 units on that chip.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Speed, opening in light speed
  • Energy, opening in 10¹² of joules

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Relativistic kinetic energy calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Testing whether an answer is physically plausible before you trust it
  • Writing up a lab result and needing a quick cross-check
  • Solving a problem set where the algebra is more interesting than the arithmetic
  • Any time the same 2 figures keep coming back — the velocity and the kinetic energy — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the Relativistic kinetic energy calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • The unit chips cover the units listed on the page. A historical or regional unit that is missing can still be used by converting it to a listed unit first.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

sections.title: How do you check the answer yourself?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time — velocity for instance — and watch which results move. A result that stays put does not depend on it.
  • Try a round value you can work out in your head. If the answer matches your mental arithmetic, the inputs are on the scale you assumed.
  • Switch the units to the ones you normally use and confirm the numbers are unchanged apart from their label; if they are not, a chip was on the wrong setting.

faq.q: What does the Relativistic kinetic energy calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns mass, derived from the velocity and the kinetic energy. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Relativistic kinetic energy calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the velocity and the kinetic energy, which is 2 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter mass in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Mass opens in kilograms and the chip beside it offers 29 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the Relativistic kinetic energy calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
